correctness.rationale: Invariance of the lifted momentum gives zero mean kick, and invariance of its second moment gives the exact half-anticovariance. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the variance bound. At equality, the affine relation makes the outgoing centered momentum the negative of the incoming one. Applying the same relation at the image forces the sine kick to reverse. Two iterates fix momentum and translate angle by twice the mean momentum. Compatibility along consecutive even iterates excludes every nonresonant mean and every half-integer-\(\pi\) alternative when kick variance is positive, leaving \(m\in\pi\mathbb Z\) and \(T^2=\mathrm{id}\) almost surely. The packaged checker verifies the exact algebra; the resonance step is proved analytically. The explicit \(K=2\pi\) two-cycle was checked exactly and attains the variance boundary.

value.rationale: The standard map is a canonical Hamiltonian-chaos model, and long chaotic trajectories can remain severely biased by stickiness for extraordinarily many iterates. The accepted theorem gives an exact, low-cost stationarity diagnostic involving the physically natural kick and lifted momentum that is independent of spatial-density equilibration. Its boundary is not merely algebraic: saturation forces mean momentum onto a half-turn resonance and collapses the full map to period at most two, so KAM-type irrational states and chaotic states with nonzero kick activity must satisfy a strict gap. That makes the result useful for distinguishing true invariant statistics from long transients in numerical standard-map studies. The explicit \(K=2\pi\) equality cycle shows that the boundary is genuinely sharp rather than only a formal obstruction.
